contract.entry: next regular-session open on/after the cutoff
contract.exit: first regular-session open on/after the calendar anniversary of the entry date; leap day clamps to Feb 28
contract.note: Game assumptions, not a reconstruction of any historical broker. Short is a simulated exposure; no recall or margin call modelled in the MVP.

benchmark_convention: SPY bought at the same entry open and sold at the same exit open, fixed shares, cash dividends in (entry, exit] added, no costs. Stock long return uses the same dates and dividend rule plus slippage.
data_note: Vendor daily bars (Yahoo chart API, cached 2026-09-09). Dividends and splits from vendor events. Not a verified corporate-action ledger.

sim.note: Client-side simulation input: fills at opens, dividends in (entry, exit], borrow on daily close. Stops and targets trigger on a close and fill at the next open.

events.headline: Daniel O'Day, former Roche Pharmaceuticals CEO, takes over as Gilead's Chairman and CEO as previously scheduled
events.detail: O'Day succeeded interim CEO Gregg Alton, who had led Gilead from January 1 to March 1, 2019, following John Milligan's retirement; the transition occurred on the date the company had announced in December 2018.

source.title: Gilead Sciences Names Daniel O'Day Chairman and Chief Executive Officer

events.opened_note: Source predates the cutoff (it is Gilead's original announcement of the transition) but is used to confirm the effective date of an event -- O'Day actually taking office -- that occurred after the cutoff, matching the catalyst named in the pre-cutoff packet.

events.headline: Gilead reports full-year 2019 revenue of $22.4 billion as Biktarvy-led HIV growth continues to outpace hepatitis C decline
events.detail: Full-year 2019 total revenue was $22.4 billion and net income was $5.4 billion ($4.22 diluted EPS); HIV sales rose to $16.4 billion from $14.6 billion on Biktarvy uptake, while hepatitis C revenue fell to $2.9 billion from $3.7 billion on lower average selling prices.

source.title: Gilead Sciences Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2019 Financial Results

events.headline: Gilead agrees to acquire Immunomedics for about $21 billion in cash to add the oncology drug Trodelvy
events.detail: Gilead agreed to pay $88.00 per share, roughly $21 billion total, for Immunomedics, whose lead product Trodelvy had recently won accelerated approval in triple-negative breast cancer; Gilead said the deal would broaden its solid-tumor pipeline and become accretive to non-GAAP EPS in 2023.

events.headline: Generic version of Gilead's HIV drug Truvada launches in the U.S. about a year earlier than the underlying patent expiry
events.detail: Teva launched an authorized generic of Truvada on September 30, 2020, under a 2014 settlement that allowed early entry; U.S. Truvada sales of roughly $2.6 billion were exposed to this competition, materializing the generic-competition risk Gilead had flagged in its 2019 guidance.

source.title: Gilead's $3B Truvada will face generics a year early. Can Descovy still win over its patients?

events.opened_note: Search-summarized only (not directly WebFetched); date and mechanism corroborated by Gilead's own FY2020 earnings release (e6), which was opened and states Truvada-based products declined due to 'loss of exclusivity in October 2020.'

events.headline: FDA grants full approval to Gilead's Veklury (remdesivir), the first approved COVID-19 treatment in the U.S.
events.detail: The approval covers hospitalized adult and pediatric COVID-19 patients 12 and older, based on the ACTT-1 trial showing a five-day faster median recovery time versus placebo; Veklury had previously been available only under emergency use authorization.

source.title: U.S. Food and Drug Administration Approves Gilead's Antiviral Veklury (remdesivir) for Treatment of COVID-19

events.headline: Gilead's full-year 2020 GAAP net income falls to $123 million even as Veklury COVID-19 sales reach $2.8 billion
events.detail: Full-year 2020 total revenue rose 10% to $24.7 billion, but GAAP net income fell to $123 million ($0.10 diluted EPS) from $5.4 billion in 2019; Veklury contributed $2.8 billion of new sales tied to pandemic hospitalizations, HIV sales grew 3% to $16.9 billion, and HCV sales fell 30% to $2.1 billion, which the company linked partly to reduced pandemic-era patient starts.

source.title: Gilead Sciences Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2020 Financial Results

events.opened_note: The opened release did not itself explain the drop from billions in net income to $123 million (likely related to acquisition accounting for Immunomedics, but that causal link was not stated in this source), so no cause is asserted here beyond the reported figures.

events.headline: FDA accepts for priority review Gilead's application to expand Trodelvy into a common, earlier-stage breast cancer type
events.detail: The FDA granted priority review to a supplemental application for Trodelvy in pre-treated HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, based on the Phase 3 TROPiCS-02 trial, with a target decision date set for February 2023.

source.title: U.S. FDA Accepts for Priority Review the Supplemental Biologics License Application for Gilead's Trodelvy for Pre-Treated HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer

events.headline: FDA approves Gilead's Sunlenca (lenacapavir), a twice-yearly injectable, for multidrug-resistant HIV
events.detail: Sunlenca was approved for heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 failing their current regimen; in the CAPELLA trial, 83% of participants receiving lenacapavir plus an optimized background regimen reached an undetectable viral load at week 52, extending Gilead's HIV franchise into a new dosing category.

source.title: Sunlenca (lenacapavir) Receives FDA Approval as a First-in-Class, Twice-Yearly Treatment Option for People Living With Multi-Drug Resistant HIV

events.headline: Gilead reports flat full-year 2022 revenue of $27.3 billion as Biktarvy tops $10 billion and Veklury sales fall 30%
events.detail: Full-year 2022 revenue was $27.3 billion, about flat versus 2021; net income attributable to Gilead was $4.6 billion ($3.64 diluted EPS) versus $6.2 billion ($4.93) in 2021, as Biktarvy sales grew 20% to $10.4 billion while Veklury sales fell 30% to $3.9 billion on fewer COVID-19 hospitalizations.

source.title: Gilead Sciences Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2022 Financial Results

events.headline: FDA approves Trodelvy for a common form of metastatic breast cancer, extending Gilead's oncology franchise beyond triple-negative disease
events.detail: The FDA approved Trodelvy for previously treated HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, a subtype accounting for an estimated 70% of new breast cancer cases, based on TROPiCS-02 data showing median survival of 14.4 versus 11.2 months for chemotherapy.

source.title: FDA approves Gilead's Trodelvy for expanded use in breast cancer

events.opened_note: Gilead's own press release for this approval returned HTTP 404 at the expected URL; BioPharma Dive's report was used instead and cross-checked against Gilead's FDA priority-review announcement (e7), which named the same February 2023 target action date.

horizon_notes.1: In the first year, the pre-cutoff packet's leading catalyst resolved on schedule: Daniel O'Day took over as Chairman and CEO on March 1, 2019 as previously announced [e1], and Gilead's full-year 2019 results, reported the following February, showed HIV revenue (led by Biktarvy) continuing to grow to $16.4 billion while hepatitis C revenue kept falling to $2.9 billion -- the same divergence the packet had described [e2]. Interpretation: the packet's framing of Biktarvy-led growth offsetting HCV decline held through the first year, but it contained no information yet on the acquisition strategy or pandemic-era product (Veklury) that would reshape the company's revenue mix over the following two years.
horizon_notes.3: Over three years, the new CEO pursued an acquisition-led diversification strategy: Gilead agreed to buy Immunomedics for about $21 billion in September 2020 to add the oncology drug Trodelvy [e3], while Truvada lost U.S. exclusivity to a generic a year earlier than expected [e4] and Veklury (remdesivir) received full FDA approval as the first approved COVID-19 treatment [e5]. Full-year 2020 revenue rose 10% to $24.7 billion on Veklury's pandemic-driven sales, even as reported GAAP net income fell sharply to $123 million [e6]. Interpretation: the packet's unresolved question about whether early-stage oncology diversification could offset HIV/HCV franchise risk was answered in part by an acquisition rather than organic pipeline progress, and neither the packet nor the market could have anticipated a pandemic creating an entirely new, large revenue line (Veklury) within the horizon.
horizon_notes.5: Across the five-year window, Gilead's oncology and HIV pipelines both advanced: Trodelvy won priority review and then approval in a much larger breast-cancer population (HR-positive, HER2-negative) beyond its original triple-negative indication [e7][e10], and the long-acting HIV drug Sunlenca was approved for multidrug-resistant patients [e8]; full-year 2022 revenue held flat at $27.3 billion as Biktarvy crossed $10 billion in sales while Veklury sales fell 30% as pandemic-era demand faded [e9]. The final year of the horizon (Feb 2023-Feb 2024) is not separately covered here -- see gaps. Interpretation: the packet's question of whether Gilead was a growth story or a value trap does not resolve cleanly either way in this record -- HIV kept growing and oncology diversification became more concrete through two acquisitions and expanded approvals, but revenue growth over the period was modest and depended partly on a non-repeatable pandemic product the pre-cutoff packet could not have foreseen.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: Gilead's full-year 2023 earnings release (Biktarvy $11.8B, oncology sales up 37%, Veklury down 44%, net income $5.7B) was published February 6, 2024 -- one day after this case's 2024-02-05 coverage boundary -- so it is described here in this note only, not as a scored event: total revenue was $27.1 billion, down 1% versus 2022.

Gilead's agreement to acquire CymaBay Therapeutics for about $4.3 billion (liver disease drug seladelpar) was announced February 12, 2024, also after the coverage boundary, so it is likewise excluded from the event list.

Because both of those items fall outside the window, the last twelve months of the five-year horizon (Feb 2023-Feb 2024) have no dedicated event in this file; the record for that period is comparatively thin.

The Truvada generic-launch event (e4) is sourced from a search summary rather than a directly opened article; its date and mechanism were corroborated against Gilead's own opened FY2020 earnings release.

The specific driver of Gilead's FY2020 GAAP net income collapse to $123 million (most likely an acquisition-related in-process R&D or intangible charge tied to Immunomedics) was not stated in the earnings release itself and is not asserted here.
Stock prices and returns are not included; the game computes those separately.

scene_check.voice: Stay away. Their hepatitis C business fell from $9 billion to under $4 billion in one year, the guidance for this year is flat to down, and they just wrote off an $820 million oncology bet. It's a value trap.

claims.text: hepatitis C product sales fell to $3.7 billion from $9.1 billion
2019 product-sales guidance of $21.3 to 21.8 billion, roughly flat to down
HIV sales rose to $14.6 billion and the company holds $31.5 billion of cash and investments

debrief_check.s1: Continued: hepatitis C fell to $2.9 billion in 2019 and kept falling, and Truvada lost US exclusivity a year early [e2][e4].
debrief_check.s2: 2019 was flat as guided. 2020 revenue rose 10% on a pandemic drug nobody could have listed at the cutoff, and 2022 revenue was flat again at $27.3 billion [e5][e6][e9].
debrief_check.s3: HIV kept growing to $16.4 billion in 2019 and Biktarvy passed $10 billion by 2022. The cash went into a $21 billion oncology acquisition [e2][e3][e9]. Compare the five-year return with SPY in the tiles above: not the trap the friend feared, and not a winner either.

assumptions.text: HIV growth will keep outrunning the hepatitis C decline.
The cash pile and new CEO will buy or build a second growth engine.
A 3x revenue multiple with $31 billion of cash is already a floor.
Generic erosion will spread from hepatitis C to HIV within five years.
My friend is right: shrinking revenue and a written-off bet make this a trap.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: HIV revenue rose to $16.4 billion in 2019 while hepatitis C fell to $2.9 billion; the lead regimen passed $10 billion by 2022 and a twice-yearly injectable was approved [e2][e8][e9]. For this assumption: supported throughout. Unknown at the cutoff: a pandemic antiviral that added a large revenue line for two years [e5][e6].
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: the new CEO bought Immunomedics for $21 billion in September 2020 to add an oncology drug, later approved in a much larger breast-cancer population [e1][e3][e7][e10]. For this assumption: supported in form. Unknown: whether the price paid earns a return; revenue was flat at $27.3 billion in 2022 [e9].
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the shares rose over five years but lagged the market by a wide margin; see the result tiles. For this assumption: a floor, not a spring. Unknown: how much the pandemic drug distorted the middle years.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: an older HIV drug lost US exclusivity a year early in 2020 [e4], yet HIV revenue kept growing on the newer regimen [e2][e9]. For this assumption: partly right on the event, wrong on the effect. Unknown: the next patent cliff, outside this window.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: revenue did not shrink further; it grew to $27.3 billion, with new products and two acquisitions [e3][e9][e10]. For this assumption: not a trap in the sense of a shrinking business; the friend's fear about the return relative to the market was closer to the mark. Unknown: what the shares would have done without the pandemic drug's two strong years.
